Bleed the Clock

There's no bell-cow to bank on — the lead back sees just 47% of carries (league ~59%), a committee that caps any one back's ceiling and makes their rushing props matchup- and script-dependent.

The Offensive Blueprint

LAC throw by design. They pass -0% over expectation (league -2%) and keep firing even with a lead (40% early-down pass when ahead vs ~41%) — the kind of pass-first identity that keeps receivers live in every script.

When they fall behind they abandon the run entirely — 63% pass while trailing, so their pass-catchers have huge comeback-script ceilings.

The WR2 is unusually involved here — 19% of targets (league ~15%), meaning there's bankable volume beyond the top receiver.

In the Red Zone

Inside the 20 they lean run-heavy, passing 50% of the time, funnelling touchdown equity to the lead back.

Defense — A Balanced Defense

They surrender 115 rushing and 212 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). No dominant funnel — read it matchup by matchup.

They lock down opposing WR2s — just 32 rec yds/game (vs ~36); fade receiving props there.

A stingy, efficient defense — just 42% success allowed (vs ~44%); temper expectations for opposing skill players.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: back their RB1's rushing volume in favored/positive scripts; their pass-catchers have massive ceilings in comeback scripts (fade-material as underdogs).

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
